t: You're looking at a statue of Edward VI inside the North Wing of St Thomas' Hospital. It's one of two statues of the king here, and both commemorate his re-founding of the hospital in 1551. This one is by Peter Scheemakers, a Flemish sculptor who worked in London for most of his life, and it was moved to its present spot in the twentieth century. Edward became king aged nine and was the first English monarch raised as a Protestant. The statue is Grade Two star listed.
